input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

An accessibility audit found that four core Dashboard flows (project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission) cannot be completed
with keyboard alone: focus is lost in modals, several controls are unreachable,
and focus indicators are inconsistent. Two public-sector customers require an
updated, published conformance statement (VPAT) before renewal — so the fixes
and the published documentation are both deliverables of this strategy.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard, with no focus traps or unreachable controls. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited flows. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed state, with technical review. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require
- Flows outside the four audited ones

## Open Questions

None — the audit report enumerates the exact defects per flow.

# Keyboard accessibility remediation for four core Dashboard flows

## Description

This epic remediates the keyboard accessibility defects found by the
accessibility audit in the four core Dashboard flows: project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, and pipeline run submission. On completion,
each of the four flows can be completed end to end with keyboard alone — no
focus traps, no unreachable controls — and visible focus indicators are
consistent across the audited flows. This delivers the code-side half of the
strategy's keyboard conformance work; the updated conformance documentation
that reflects this fixed state is delivered separately.

## Scope

- Remediate every defect enumerated in the accessibility audit report for the
  four audited flows, including:
  - focus loss and focus traps in modals opened during the flows;
  - controls that are unreachable via keyboard (cannot be focused or activated
    without a pointer);
  - inconsistent or missing visible focus indicators on interactive controls.
- Make each of the four flows fully operable by keyboard alone, from entry
  through completion of the flow, including cancel/dismiss paths.
- Apply a consistent focus-indicator treatment across the audited flows'
  interactive controls so focus state is visibly uniform.
- Keep the fixes within the four audited flows and within keyboard-related
  behavior: screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require,
  and flows outside the four audited ones, are out of scope per the strategy.
- Update any screenshots, captions, or references in existing test fixtures or
  documentation that directly fall out of these changes (incidental
  touch-ups only — no new documentation content).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the project creation flow, when it is operated end to end using only
  the keyboard, then every step can be completed, no focus trap occurs, and no
  control is unreachable.
- Given the workbench spawn flow, when it is operated end to end using only
  the keyboard, then every step can be completed, no focus trap occurs, and no
  control is unreachable.
- Given the model deployment flow, when it is operated end to end using only
  the keyboard, then every step can be completed, no focus trap occurs, and no
  control is unreachable.
- Given the pipeline run submission flow, when it is operated end to end using
  only the keyboard, then every step can be completed, no focus trap occurs,
  and no control is unreachable.
- Given the interactive controls across the four audited flows, when an
  element receives keyboard focus, then a visible focus indicator is shown
  with a consistent treatment across all four flows.
- Every defect enumerated in the audit report for the four flows is addressed
  or explicitly dispositioned with rationale in the epic's completion record.
- The existing automated test suite passes and the Dashboard's existing build
  pipeline is green with these changes; keyboard fixes do not regress
  pointer-based interaction in the four flows.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P1)** — The four audited core flows are fully operable by
  keyboard, with no focus traps or unreachable controls: covered by this
  epic's flow-by-flow keyboard operability acceptance criteria.
- **HLR-2 (P1)** — Visible focus indicators are consistent across the
  audited flows: covered by this epic's consistent focus-indicator scope and
  acceptance criterion.

## Risks/Notes

- **Size estimate and re-split trigger**: this epic spans four flows and is
  estimated at roughly one sprint (~10 working days) of Dashboard engineering
  effort. It is kept as one epic because it is a single logical change — the
  same three defect classes (modal focus traps, unreachable controls,
  inconsistent focus indicators) remediated across audit-enumerated targets
  with a shared focus-indicator treatment; splitting per flow would duplicate
  the shared treatment and fragment one audit-remediation pass. Conditional
  re-split trigger: if the audit defect volume or elapsed effort exceeds one
  sprint (i.e., the epic is not code-complete within a single sprint), split
  it along the per-flow seam into one epic per audited flow, keeping the
  shared focus-indicator treatment in the first of them.

# Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and accessibility statement)

## Description

This epic updates and republishes the accessibility conformance documentation
to reflect the fixed state of the four core Dashboard flows after the keyboard
accessibility remediation lands. It covers the updated VPAT (Voluntary
Product Accessibility Template) conformance statement and the product
documentation accessibility statement. The updated documents are technically
reviewed against the actual implemented behavior before republication, so the
published conformance claims match what was built.

## Scope

Content outline:

- **VPAT update**: revise the existing published VPAT so the entries for the
  four audited flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment,
  pipeline run submission) reflect keyboard operability and focus-indicator
  conformance after remediation; keep claims scoped to what the fixes
  actually deliver and consistent with the strategy's out-of-scope list (no
  claims about screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes
  require, and none about flows outside the four audited ones).
- **Product docs accessibility statement update**: revise the existing
  accessibility statement in the product documentation to describe the current
  conformance state, including any documented limitations that remain outside
  this strategy's scope.
- **Republish**: push the updated VPAT and accessibility statement through
  the Red Hat docs content process so the published versions reflect the
  fixed state.
- **Technical review**: have the updated conformance claims reviewed by the
  engineering owners of the keyboard remediation to confirm every claim is
  accurate against the implemented behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The VPAT is updated so its entries for the four audited flows accurately
  reflect the post-remediation keyboard operability and focus-indicator
  state, with no claims extending beyond the delivered fixes.
- The product documentation accessibility statement is updated to describe
  the current conformance state, including explicitly documented remaining
  limitations outside this strategy's scope.
- The updated VPAT and accessibility statement are technically reviewed
  against the implemented keyboard accessibility behavior, and the review
  confirms every conformance claim is accurate; review findings are
  incorporated before publication.
- The updated VPAT and accessibility statement are republished — the publicly
  available versions reflect the fixed state of the four flows.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P2)** — The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and
  product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect
  the fixed state, with technical review: covered entirely by this epic's
  scope and acceptance criteria.

## Risks / Notes

- Two public-sector customers require the republished conformance statement
  before their renewal; the renewal dates are externally controlled schedule
  constraints, not deliverables of this epic — the epic's controllable
  completion point is the reviewed, republished documentation.
